name: Buzz
description: Self-host Buzz, Block's hive-mind workspace for humans and AI agents. Includes the relay with bundled web UI, Postgres, Redis, and S3-compatible media storage.

PORT.description: The port the Buzz server listens on inside its container. Leave this alone.

BUZZ_RELAY_PRIVATE_KEY.description: The private identity of the server itself, generated fresh for your deployment. Never share it and never change it after launch.

BUZZ_GIT_HOOK_HMAC_SECRET.description: A shared password that lets your code repositories prove that git updates really came from them. Generated fresh for your deployment.

BUZZ_CORS_ORIGINS.description: Which websites are allowed to talk to your Buzz server from a browser. Defaults to your own domain, which is what you want.

BUZZ_MEDIA_BASE_URL.description: The public web address that uploaded images and files are served from. Filled in automatically from this service's domain.

RELAY_URL.description: The public address other people and apps use to reach your Buzz server. Filled in automatically from this service's domain.

BUZZ_PAIRING_RELAY_URL.description: The public address of the mobile-pairing helper service, advertised to the desktop app so 'Pair Mobile Device' works. Filled in automatically from the Pairing service's domain.

BUZZ_S3_ENDPOINT.description: Where Buzz stores uploaded files and images. Points at the private address of the MinIO service. Filled in automatically.

BUZZ_S3_SECRET_KEY.description: The password Buzz uses to reach its file storage. Copied automatically from the MinIO service.

DATABASE_URL.description: Where Buzz finds its Postgres database. Filled in automatically from the Postgres service.

REDIS_URL.description: Where Buzz finds its Redis cache. Filled in automatically from the Redis service.

RELAY_OWNER_PUBKEY.description: Your Buzz public key goes here. New to Buzz? (1) Download the app from github.com/block/buzz/releases/latest and open it. (2) Choose 'Create a new identity key'. (3) On the next screen ('Join a community'), click the 'Copy your public ID' button. (4) Paste it here. It starts with 'npub' and is safe to share, like an email address. Full walkthrough with pictures: hmseeb.github.io/buzz-railway#setup . When the deploy finishes, open this service's URL in a browser and click 'Open in Buzz' to connect the app. Don't want to install the app first? Type the word generate and a key is made for you.

PORT.description: The port the pairing helper listens on inside its container. Leave this alone.

BUZZ_PAIR_RELAY_BIND_ADDR.description: The address the pairing helper listens on. Filled in automatically. Leave this alone.

PGDATA.description: The folder on disk where the database keeps your data. Leave this alone.

POSTGRES_DB.description: The name of the database created on first launch.

POSTGRES_PASSWORD.description: The database password, generated fresh for your deployment. Never share it.

POSTGRES_USER.description: The database account created on first launch.

REDIS_PASSWORD.description: The cache password, generated fresh for your deployment. Never share it.

REDIS_URL.description: The full private connection details for the cache, assembled from the other settings here. This is what Buzz actually reads.

PORT.description: The port the file storage service listens on inside its container. Leave this alone.

MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD.description: The admin password for your file storage. Generated fresh for your deployment. Buzz picks it up automatically.

MINIO_DOMAIN.description: The private address other services use to reach file storage. Filled in automatically.
